key_insight: KKT-HardNet combines neural-network inference with a differentiable projection layer to enforce algebraic physical constraints in physics-constrained machine learning.
engineering_relevance: Its modular framework supports hybrid modeling, process simulation, optimization, and model predictive control within one platform.
method: Project neural-network outputs to satisfy linear and nonlinear equality and inequality constraints.
Use implicit-function-theorem gradients for end-to-end training through the projection layer.
Support custom backbones and projection mechanisms, including reduced-order Fischer–Burmeister reformulation and primal-dual interior-point solving.
evidence_signal: Across engineering benchmarks, the abstract reports orders-of-magnitude improvements in constraint satisfaction and inference time; code and benchmark datasets are publicly available.
watch_item: Practical constraint enforcement depends on projection-solver convergence and numerical tolerances, which are not detailed in the abstract.
paper_title: A Tutorial on Physics Constrained Machine Learning for Hybrid Modeling, Optimization, and Control
